author: pilot_suggester

checks.description: Measure one full logical read with the independently matching archive digest.
Retain corruption/truncation/read-error and existing export/UI/filesystem guarantees.

constraints.text: Retain reproducible before/after measurements for the exact specified fixture. Count all underlying verification reads, including buffering/read-ahead, headers and trailing padding. The after-change path must consume exactly 9,123,840 logical bytes once and return the independent whole-file SHA-256, without a separate digest scan or whole-archive memory buffer. Drain to EOF even after tar member iteration finishes.

Keep payload and manifest digest checks, duplicate/unexpected-member rejection and bounded buffering. Test real malformed/corrupt headers or payloads, truncation including final padding, and read errors during the final drain. These failures must prevent publication. Validate complete read length against the completed archive size so semantic success before EOF cannot conceal truncation.

Preserve held-destination access, source/media revalidation, no-replace publication, fsync failure handling and operation-owned partial-file cleanup. Retain source and existing-destination preservation, long Unicode/PAX names, directories, manifests, sparse-file budgets and SQLite/WAL coverage, and rerun the approved provider's actual GTK/FAT workflow. Keep physical media and power-loss acceptance in the parent recovery feature and canonical human checklist.

decision.rationale: The improvement is supported by current runtime/sv08_export.py: execute performs a complete digest scan, then verify_archive rereads archive members. Independent in-memory reproduction produced the proposed 9,123,840-byte archive and SHA-256 0767efa76615052ca0c1506ec6c76bbdeee2ce989c44dfa5aff434872102aa72, with 9,123,840 digest bytes plus 9,119,075 semantic bytes, totaling 18,242,915 logical bytes. Combining complete digest and semantic verification removes demonstrated redundant reads without a format, dependency or hardware change. The dependency on recovery-media-export:implement is appropriate for end-to-end regression coverage. Approval concerns logical read volume and offline integrity only; it establishes neither physical throughput nor power-loss durability.

evidence.limitations: Workstation fixtures and selected ARM64 Python under QEMU only. No physical printer/media, complete recovery image, power-loss or throughput acceptance; canonical physical tasks remain blocked.
evidence.method: Reproduced the exact approved archive and baseline source: 18,242,915 to 9,123,840 underlying logical bytes, matching independent SHA-256, zero seeks and one EOF read. Real export test forbids writer reads and counts the single readback.

evidence.limitations: Workstation fixtures and selected ARM64 Python under QEMU only. No physical printer/media, complete recovery image, power-loss or throughput acceptance; canonical physical tasks remain blocked.
evidence.method: 53 targeted workstation tests, 34 selected ARM64 runtime tests, actual GTK directory workflow and real provider GTK/ext4/FAT32 fixture passed. Corruption, final-drain errors, metadata/sparse bounds, source/media preservation, cancellation, shared exclusion and publication failures covered; fresh payload staging measured.

verification.rationale: Verified the complete eight-file diff from fd4d143 to 2a50af2289650b04263d47b6859665d0416c56e0, clean HEAD, all submitted document/source hashes, and the complete approved decision. Independently reproduced the exact fixture on workstation Python 3.12.3 and selected ARM64 Python 3.13.5: verification reads fall from 18,242,915 to 9,123,840 bytes with the approved SHA-256, zero seeks and one EOF read. Independently passed 29 export-related tests, 9 media tests, 34 ARM64 runtime tests and the actual GTK directory workflow. Reviewed the real provider GTK/ext4/FAT fixture and confirmed its retained result matches the sanitized evidence, including cancellation, exclusion, preservation, removal and device-reuse checks. Corruption, metadata changes, payload/manifest mismatches, truncation, appended bytes and final-drain errors prevent publication. Sparse expansion and invalid member sizes are rejected before extraction; bounded metadata parsing and existing Unicode/PAX, directory, sparse-source and SQLite/WAL behavior remain covered. Held-destination access, source/media revalidation, no-replace publication and fsync/cleanup guards are preserved. Staging hashes and byte totals match the recorded revisions; JSON, local Markdown paths, diff checks and indexed gitlinks agree. No material findings remain. Approval covers offline logical-read and integrity behavior only; physical media, input, power-loss and complete recovery-image acceptance remain explicitly blocked in the parent feature and canonical checklist.
